UX RESEARCH CASE STUDY

Standardizing Feature Releases at TOPdesk

Transforming ad-hoc processes into strategic, repeatable systems

Role
UX Researcher
Duration
3 Months
Methods
Interviews, Workshops, Affinity Mapping
Impact
Cross-organizational Strategy

Note: This project was completed in collaboration with team members at TOPdesk. The research and design work represents a collaborative effort.

OVERVIEW

The Challenge

TOPdesk's feature releases lacked standardization, creating a ripple effect of problems: inconsistent user experiences, burdened UX teams reinventing processes, and development efforts that failed to generate expected adoption.

Our product's feature releases lack a standardized approach

This wasn't just an operational inefficiency—it was actively undermining product value, team productivity, and customer satisfaction.

THE STAKES

Why This Matters

🎯 User Adoption at Risk

Without consistent communication and onboarding, users struggle to discover and adopt new features, directly reducing ROI on development investments.

⚙️ Team Efficiency Compromised

UX designers and researchers spend excessive time reinventing release processes for each feature instead of focusing on innovation.

🚀 Development Velocity Slowed

Product teams face significant bottlenecks from lack of standardized workflows, delaying time-to-market for critical features.

METHODOLOGY

Research Approach

1

Discovery Workshop

Collaborative session with UX researchers across product teams to map current practices, decision factors, and identify gaps in existing processes.

2

Stakeholder Interviews

In-depth conversations with 7 key stakeholders: 4 Product Owners/Managers, 2 User Guidance team members, and 1 Copywriter.

3

Affinity Mapping

Systematic synthesis of research data, clustering insights into actionable categories and identifying patterns across teams.

Research Questions

  • What are the current processes and steps when introducing new features?
  • What challenges do different teams face during feature introductions?
  • How do stakeholders currently communicate and collaborate?
  • What are the main pain points or bottlenecks delaying releases?
RESEARCH SYNTHESIS

From Raw Data to Insights

Our affinity mapping process transformed hundreds of interview notes into structured, actionable insights:

Affinity Mapping Session: Clustering interview insights from 7 stakeholders into four main categories: Communication, Solutions, Release Notes, and Additional Tags
INSIGHTS

Key Findings

Through affinity mapping, insights emerged across four critical categories:

Categorized Findings: Research insights organized into Communication, Solutions, Release Notes, and Small Tags

1. Communication Fragmentation

  • Way of Working: Product Owners drive strategy but collaboration happens inconsistently between teams and departments
  • Channel Confusion: External communication channels (What's New, emails, blog posts) differ drastically from internal ones
  • Information Overload: When new channels are added, users stop checking them and fall out of the loop

2. Process Standardization Gaps

  • No Shared Approach: Development teams build everything from scratch with no standardized templates or guidelines
  • Time Drain: UX teams spend excessive time creating solutions for each release instead of reusing proven patterns
  • Inconsistent Quality: Without standards, release quality varies significantly across teams

3. Documentation Challenges

  • Technical Overload: Documentation portal often too detailed and technical for average users
  • Timing Issues: Portal can only be updated after release, missing critical onboarding window
  • Balance Struggle: Teams can't find the right balance between comprehensive detail and accessibility

4. Measurement & Feedback

  • No Standard Metrics: Lack of standardized methods for measuring user satisfaction post-release
  • PO Dependency: Release decisions heavily dependent on individual Product Owner preferences
  • Scattered Cooperation: Technical writers collaborate with dev teams, but processes vary
CURRENT STATE

Mapping the Existing Process

We documented the current release strategy and journey to understand the existing state and identify opportunities for improvement:

Release Strategy Flow: Current decision points, touchpoints, and communication paths in the feature release process
Release Journey Map: End-to-end view of stakeholder activities, pain points, and opportunities throughout the release lifecycle

The Bottom Line

By standardizing the feature release process, TOPdesk can transform from ad-hoc release management to a strategic, repeatable system. This research provides the foundation for improving customer satisfaction, team efficiency, and product competitiveness—turning internal process improvement into measurable business value.
